title: Zenoti Alternative for Wellness Clinics (October 2026)
summary: Looking for a Zenoti alternative for wellness clinics? Compare what to check on labs, charting, CRM and group events before you switch.
body_markdown:
## Why Do Wellness Clinics Look for a Zenoti Alternative?


Wellness clinics usually look for a Zenoti alternative because the product was designed for a different business.[Zenoti](https://www.zenoti.com/) says it serves more than 30,000 salon, spa and medspa businesses in over 50 countries, and its verticals are salon, barbershop, medspa and fitness. A clinic that books a hormone consult, draws labs and sells a monthly IV membership sits at the edge of that picture.


The complaints we hear from operators on sales calls fall into four groups:


- The system is learnable, but only by people who use it all day. A one-person admin runs into a wall.
- Medical records are typed in or attached as images. A client cannot send a lab history and have it organized.
- Email and text campaigns have to be built and customized from scratch, and the clinic ends up paying for a separate marketing tool on top.
- Patient messages land in one inbox that every staff member sees, so there is no simple way to answer one patient from that patient's record.


Competitor blogs repeat a fifth complaint, which is cost.[Pabau](https://pabau.com/blog/zenoti-competitors/) and[GlossGenius](https://glossgenius.com/blog/zenoti-alternatives) both describe quote-based pricing that rises with locations and add-ons, and GlossGenius cites annual contracts that are hard to exit. Both are written by vendors that sell against Zenoti, so verify those points yourself, and note that both also credit Zenoti with strong reporting and multi-location control.


## What Should a Wellness Clinic Test Before Leaving Zenoti?


Test five workflows, in your own demo account if the vendor will allow it, and do not accept a slide as an answer. They are lab ordering and trending, medical charting, patient messaging and marketing, rooms and equipment, and group events. Each one is a place where a spa-first platform and a clinic-first platform behave differently, and each one decides how many tools you keep paying for after the switch.


Workflow What to ask the vendor to show live What a weak answer sounds like


Labs Order a panel, receive a result, and trend one value across three draws "You can upload a PDF to the chart"


Medical charting Write a visit note from a template, sign it, and pull an old note back up Notes live as free text attached to the appointment


Messaging and CRM Text one patient from their profile, then build a win-back campaign A separate marketing tool is needed for campaigns


Rooms and equipment Block a cold plunge and an IV chair so two patients cannot double-book it Only providers can be booked


Group events Create a 20-seat Wednesday session that closes when full "We can work around that"


Hold the vendor to the same script. A demo that shows you the calendar for twenty minutes and skips the labs has told you something.


## How Should Labs Work in a Wellness Clinic Platform?


Labs should work as ordering, results and trending in one place, not as a folder of attachments. The practical test is whether a testosterone or A1C value from March and one from October appear on the same chart without anyone retyping them. If the answer is "upload the PDF," your provider is still comparing results by eye.


The owner above described the problem plainly. A client cannot send over a lab history and have it organized, so the staff types values in or saves a screenshot, and nothing trends. In Decoda Health, lab orders route through your own Quest or LabCorp account, the patient walks into a service center where the order is already waiting, and results return as structured data that can be trended against previous draws. The[lab ordering and results product page](https://decodahealth.com/products/labs) shows the flow, and[our guide to EMR lab integration](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-emr-lab-integration) lists the questions to ask any vendor before you sign.


If you track body composition or wearables as well,[linking InBody scans and wearable data to the chart](https://decodahealth.com/blog/wearables-inbody-lab-emr-weight-loss-clinic) is the same structured-data question. Ask the vendor whether the data lands in the record or in a separate app.


## What Does Medical Charting Need to Include?


Medical charting for a wellness clinic needs templates by treatment, vitals and measurements, photos, medication administration and a signed note, all tied to the patient record. Zenoti lists forms, charting and an AI scribe among its features, so the question is depth, not presence: can a nurse practitioner chart an IV visit and a hormone follow-up the way she would in a clinical EMR?


Check three things. First, can you build your own note templates, or only edit the vendor's? Second, does the note sit on the patient's timeline with every earlier note, or only on the appointment? Third, does the AI scribe cost extra? Comparison pages from[our Boulevard alternatives guide](https://decodahealth.com/blog/boulevard-software-alternatives) already note that Zenoti's scribe is priced as a separate add-on, so include it when you compare quotes. For the wider evaluation, see[how to select wellness clinic software](https://decodahealth.com/blog/wellness-clinic-software-selection) .


## Do You Still Need a Separate CRM?


You should not need one. A wellness clinic's marketing is mostly lists: patients due for a recall, members who lapsed, leads who never booked, people with a birthday this month. When the patient record and the campaign tool are separate, someone exports a list, imports it, and hopes the unsubscribe flags match. The owner we spoke with had already tried a general-purpose marketing platform and was walking away from it because it did not do what it promised.


The test is simple: pick a group inside the patient record, send them a text, and see who booked afterward without leaving the system. Decoda Health's[growth and CRM tools](https://decodahealth.com/products/growth) and[patient records](https://decodahealth.com/products/patients) sit in the same platform for that reason, and the individual patient thread shows texts, emails and calls in one place.


One caution for any stack. If patient messages pass through a marketing tool that is not your EMR, that vendor is handling protected health information on your behalf, and HHS requires a business associate agreement with it. The agency's[sample business associate provisions](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/sample-business-associate-agreement-provisions/index.html) are a good reference when you ask a vendor whether they will sign one.


## How Do Rooms, Equipment and Group Events Work?


Rooms and equipment should be bookable resources with their own capacity, separate from providers. A wellness clinic with six IV chairs, two cold plunges and a cryo chamber needs the calendar to stop a seventh IV booking and a second plunge booking in the same slot. Decoda Health's[scheduling product](https://decodahealth.com/products/scheduling) treats rooms and equipment this way, with a capacity setting, and a service that needs the laser room cannot be booked without it.


Group events are different, and this is where we would be careful with any vendor, ours included. A fixed-seat session, such as a Wednesday evening group for 20 people that closes when full, is not the same thing as a room with six chairs. Operators coming off appointment-first systems tell us it cannot be done there. Ask each vendor to build your exact event during the demo: the seat cap, the sign-up page, the payment and what happens at seat 21. If the answer is a configuration the vendor will do for you before go-live, get that in writing with the date.

## Why Decoda Health Fits Wellness Clinics That Outgrew Zenoti


Decoda Health fits a clinic that wants the calendar, the chart, labs, memberships and patient messaging in one system without a separate CRM. It is built for cash-pay elective care, which includes IV therapy, hormone programs, weight loss and longevity practices, and it is not built for insurance-heavy practices that bill thousands of claims a month.


The pieces that matter to the clinics we hear from:


- **Memberships and packages:** recurring plans and prepaid credits, described on the[memberships page](https://decodahealth.com/products/memberships) .
- **AI front desk:** calls and texts answered around the clock, covered on the[AI front desk page](https://decodahealth.com/products/ai-front-desk) .
- **Migration:** Decoda Health runs the migration and guarantees it in 3-4 weeks.[What transfers in an EMR migration](https://decodahealth.com/blog/med-spa-emr-migration-what-transfers) explains what moves and what gets rebuilt.


## How Should You Time the Switch Around Your Zenoti Contract?


Start with the renewal date. If your term runs to January, as it did for the owner above, the real deadline is the notice window before it, which the contract sets, so read the text instead of relying on memory. Missing it can renew you for another term.


A workable plan runs in four steps. Book demos now and ask every vendor for a written quote with onboarding, texting, scribe and extra locations itemized. Choose by early November if you want to be live before year end. Spend the middle weeks on configuration and staff training while Zenoti keeps running. Cut over the week the old term ends, and keep the old system read-only for a month so you can check a sample of records. A 3-4 week migration leaves room for that, a slower one does not.


## Final Thoughts on Choosing a Zenoti Alternative


If you run a wellness clinic and spend your week fighting the software, write down the five workflows above, ask every vendor to run them live, and decide on what you see. Zenoti is a serious platform for the businesses it was designed for, and the right alternative depends on whether your revenue looks more like a spa or more like a clinic.


If it looks like a clinic, book a walkthrough of Decoda Health at[our demo link](https://calendly.com/d/cr5z-78z-8zq/decoda-ai-intro) and bring your own lab, charting and group-event scenarios.


## Frequently Asked Questions


What is the best Zenoti alternative for a wellness clinic?


It depends on how clinical your services are. A clinic that sells IV therapy, hormones, lab panels or weight loss needs charting, lab ordering and prescribing in the same system as the calendar, so look at medical platforms such as Decoda Health or Pabau. A clinic that is closer to a spa, with classes and retail, may be better served by Mindbody or Vagaro. Shortlist two and demo your own workflow in each.


Why do wellness clinics leave Zenoti?


The reasons operators give are consistent: the software is hard to learn without dedicated training, labs and outside records have to be typed in or attached as images, marketing automation takes heavy setup, and pricing is quote-based. Zenoti does serve large multi-location groups well, so the complaint is usually fit rather than quality. A small clinic pays for enterprise depth it does not use.


How long does it take to switch from Zenoti to another platform?


Plan for weeks, not days, and start before your contract ends. Decoda Health guarantees a 3-4 week migration that it runs itself. The calendar, patient list, memberships and packages move first, and clinical history is reviewed with you before go-live. Whatever vendor you pick, ask for the cutover date in writing and keep your old system read-only until you have checked a sample of records.


Does Zenoti publish its pricing?


No. Zenoti's website does not list plan prices, and comparison articles from competing vendors report quote-based pricing that varies with locations, providers and add-ons. Treat those third-party figures as unverified. Ask Zenoti and every alternative for a written quote that includes onboarding, texting, AI scribe and any extra locations, so you compare the same scope.


Can I run group events and support groups in a wellness clinic platform?


Not every platform handles a fixed-seat group event, such as a Wednesday evening session with 20 spots. Operators who have used appointment-first systems report workarounds. Ask each vendor to build your exact event live in the demo, including the seat cap, the waitlist and the payment. Rooms and equipment with a capacity setting, like a six-chair IV lounge, are a separate and more common feature.


Should I wait for my Zenoti contract to end before switching?


Not necessarily, but read the contract first. Find the renewal date and the notice window, since a missed window can renew you for another term. Many clinics use the final two or three months to configure and train on the new system, then cut over the week the old term ends, so they never pay for two systems longer than they have to.
